top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) rests on a clear new principle, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, which is understood quantitatively by light-shift theory. It has been reproduced and surpassed independently at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE, and it now yields physics about nature (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, constraints on constants, dark-matter searches). It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and the two-name allocation was proposed identically by every member. The remaining weaknesses are that it is an invention and measurement capability, and that parallel contributions are left out. I judge these do not outweigh a mature, confirmed achievement, so awarding it is better than no award.
